record.paper_title: Open problems in nuclear structure near drip lines
record.context_brief: Halo and skin constraints on dilute matter
record.original_question: What information about dilute neutron matter and asymmetric nuclear matter can be inferred from finite neutron-rich nuclei near the neutron drip line? In particular, can observed neutron halos and neutron skins be used to extract properties of dilute neutron matter, determine the symmetry energy of asymmetric nuclear matter, and quantify how strongly low-density matter properties are manifested in finite nuclei whose outer neutron density is far below normal nuclear saturation density?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to extract information on dilute neutron matter from the observed properties of the neutron halo and skin? Can we obtain the symmetry energy of asymmetric nuclear matter? How significantly are these matter properties manifested by finite nuclei? These are still open questions to answer.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider asymmetric nuclear matter, an idealized infinite system of neutrons and protons with neutron density $\rho_n$ and proton density $\rho_p$, total density $\rho=\rho_n+\rho_p$, and isospin asymmetry $\delta=(\rho_n-\rho_p)/\rho$. The energy per nucleon admits the expansion $E(\rho,\delta)/A = E_0(\rho)+S(\rho)\,\delta^2+O(\delta^4)$, where $S(\rho)$ is the nuclear symmetry energy and the saturation density is $\rho_0\approx 0.16\,\mathrm{fm}^{-3}$. Pure neutron matter at densities $\rho_n\ll\rho_0$ is referred to as dilute neutron matter. In finite neutron-rich nuclei near the neutron drip line, the outermost neutrons form either a neutron halo (a low-density tail produced by weakly bound neutrons extending far beyond the proton distribution) or a neutron skin (an excess of neutrons over protons in the nuclear surface region), characterized by the skin thickness $\Delta R_{np}=\langle r^2\rangle_n^{1/2}-\langle r^2\rangle_p^{1/2}$, with the local neutron density in these surface regions far below $\rho_0$.

Address the following:
(a) Determine to what extent the measured properties of neutron halos and neutron skins in finite neutron-rich nuclei near the drip line can be used to extract quantitative information about the equation of state of dilute neutron matter.
(b) Determine whether such observations can be used to constrain or determine the symmetry energy $S(\rho)$ of asymmetric nuclear matter (including its value at saturation and its density slope $L=3\rho_0\,dS/d\rho|_{\rho_0}$).
(c) Quantify how strongly the bulk properties of low-density nuclear and neutron matter are manifested in the observable properties of finite nuclei whose outermost neutron density is well below saturation.
artifact.category_tag: Nuclear structure and equation of state
artifact.status_search_result: The relationship between neutron skins/halos and the symmetry energy and dilute neutron matter equation of state remains an active research problem. Recent works (2024–2025) continue to investigate constraints on the symmetry energy slope L from neutron skin measurements (notably the CREX/PREX-II tension on $^{48}$Ca and $^{208}$Pb), with no consensus yet, and explicitly link the resolution to the dilute-matter equation of state.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry energy in dilute matter and the neutron skin
status_evidence.snippet: The puzzle of reconciling CREX and PREX-II results can be resolved by revisiting the nuclear surface, as driven in part by the EoS in dilute matter well below saturation.
status_evidence.claim: The connection between dilute matter EoS and neutron skin remains an open, actively studied problem in 2025.

status_evidence.title: The nuclear symmetry energy and the neutron skin thickness in nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Review of constraints on slope parameter L from neutron skin thicknesses of 48Ca and 208Pb; sensitivity issues remain unresolved.
status_evidence.claim: Extracting the symmetry energy from neutron skins remains an open problem with model-dependent results.

status_evidence.title: New quantification of symmetry energy from neutron skin
status_evidence.snippet: Recent quantification studies show ongoing tension between extractions of L from different nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus yet on extraction of symmetry energy from finite nuclei observables.
